verified.entry_point: The real edge handlers and executor that act on cloud-supplied node operations jobs: the v1alpha2 upgrade, config-update and image pre-pull actions (driven through the ActionRunner, including the save-then-reload route the metaserver confirm-upgrade endpoint uses), and the legacy v1alpha1 upgrade/rollback task executor (driven through its registered states). Nothing is stubbed: the suites build the real ActionRunner and Executor, use the real SQLite meta_v2 store for the save/reload route, and put recorder scripts named keadm/crictl on PATH so the tests can read, as data, the exact arguments the edge hands to the tools.
variants: base (published fix, pattern A): the v1alpha2 upgrade action concatenates the job's version and image into a `bash -c` line; a value with `;` or `$()` runs an extra command on the node.

producer/reload (how, the main lever): the job spec is stored by the runner's pre-run hook before the check action runs, and the confirm-upgrade endpoint reloads it and starts the flow at BackUp, so Upgrade executes without the check; a fix that validates only in the check step leaves this open.
far site (published fix, pattern A): the legacy v1alpha1 executor builds `nohup keadm ... <request fields>` through bash; a fix limited to the v1alpha2 action changes nothing there.
uncovered route (pattern B, real upstream): the config-update action joins UpdateFields keys and values into `keadm config-update --set` through bash; the published fix never touches it.
injected sibling (image pre-pull check): a submitted image list is probed with `crictl inspecti <image>` through bash in the pre-pull check action (our copy only; inject.patch).
injected sibling (recovery cleanup): the failed-upgrade directory, derived from the request version, is removed with `rm -rf <path>` through bash in the legacy rollback (our copy only; inject.patch).
verified.project_tests_run: At image build time the pinned project tests for the affected area pass: go test ./pkg/util/validation ./pkg/nodetask/actionflow ./cloud/pkg/admissioncontroller, plus the non-patching TestRunAction in ./edge/pkg/taskmanager/actions, after `go build ./pkg/util/validation ./pkg/nodetask/actionflow ./edge/pkg/taskmanager/...` compiles the whole affected tree. The pinned edge/pkg/taskmanager/actions tests that use gomonkey assert the vulnerable command line itself and are rewritten by the upstream fix; they are build-time proof only (verified passing at pin with -gcflags=all=-l in a scratch checkout) and the two packages that host hidden tests are staged with only the hidden files at grade time. The graded functional group re-runs the pristine pkg/util/validation and pkg/nodetask/actionflow project tests.

traps.shape: the published fix's protected sink: the job's version and image are concatenated into a bash command line in the v1alpha2 upgrade action
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none needed - this is the value the report shows and the obvious place to repair

traps.pattern: A (how: producer off the check's path)
traps.shape: the runner stores the spec before the check action; the confirm-upgrade endpoint reloads that stored spec and starts the flow at BackUp, so the Upgrade action executes without the check ever seeing the value
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the confirmation route replays a spec the edge itself stored, so both the data and the route read as already trusted; the visible check step is where the report points
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the save hook, the store and the confirm endpoint exist at the pinned commit; the security suite drives the same save -> reload -> Upgrade action sequence the endpoint uses

traps.shape: the legacy v1alpha1 executor builds a bash command line from the request's IDs, version, image and config path and runs it with nohup
traps.reason_to_dismiss: deprecated legacy API; the advisory names the v1alpha2 flow, and upstream those fields are a validated object name, a UUID and a semver-checked version, so the path reads as already constrained

traps.shape: the config-update action joins an update map's keys and values into `keadm config-update --set <pairs>` and runs it through bash
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a different CRD and feature (configuration update, not upgrade); the values look like plain key=value settings, and the advisory names only the upgrade job
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit; the published fix never touches the file

traps.shape: the pre-pull check action probes each submitted image with a shell `crictl inspecti <image>` line
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a different job kind (pre-pull); image references read as identifiers, and the probe only inspects a local cache
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer adding a local-cache probe in this package would reuse the execs.NewCommand(fmt.Sprintf(...)) style used by the neighbouring actions; INJECTED into our copy only, registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

traps.shape: the legacy rollback removes the failed upgrade's directory, derived from the request version, with a shell `rm -rf <path>` line
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the failure-recovery branch of the legacy API; the code only cleans a directory derived from a version string, which reads as local path handling
traps.realistic_because: the file already builds its recovery command with fmt.Sprintf + bash; a maintainer cleaning the failed upgrade directory in the same style is a one-screen change; INJECTED into our copy only, registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

traps.shape: the legitimate values next to the sink: registry:port, tag, digest, empty image, prerelease version, several config pairs, a detached logged legacy upgrade, and the probe/cleanup behaviour itself
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the quick repair is to reject anything unusual in the value ('':'','@'), require an image, or drop the shell-out feature entirely; each of those breaks behaviour the product has today
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: the failure mode is an over-broad fix, proved by func_overbroad.patch (expect functional_fail)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the security tests assert only that the marker file is absent and never require an error value; a panic aborts the Go test and an os.Exit loses the suite's results, so a crash can never be scored as a refusal
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is a single protected resource (the command line the edge builds for a job); no neighbouring or proxy resource exists that a fix could authorise by mistake
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the sink has no roles, peers or directions; every value of a job reaches the same command line
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no offset, clamp, unit conversion or normalisation sits between the check and the executed value; the reference fix removes the shell rather than moving the check
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the values are free text and no identity string is parsed into fields where a malformed spelling could slip past a comparison
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: confinement is structural (pass values as argv, or validate an allow-list); no external authority can fail open
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the fixes are per call site; the shared validators are additive and no neighbouring API's stated behaviour depends on them
